newsitem.title: POLAND: YOUNG JEWS STAGE MARCH OF LIVING AT AUSCHWITZ.
newsitem.headline: YOUNG JEWS STAGE MARCH OF LIVING AT AUSCHWITZ.

text.p: Some 2,500 young Jews from around the world marked world Holocaust Day my staging a March of the Living at the site of Nazi Germany's biggest death camp in southern Poland.

The youths, mainly from Israel, Canada and the United States, marched from the site of the former Auschwitz concentration camp in the southern town of Oswiecim to nearby Birkenau, where most of the complex's 1.5 million victims were killed.
About 90 percent of those put to death in the Auschwitz-Birkenau complex were Jewish, many of them brought in from all over Europe.
Many of those participating in the annual event heard the names of their ancestors, who perished at the world's major Holocaust site, read out.
The Kadish, the traditional Jewish prayer for the dead, was recited at the International Memorial to Victims of Fascism near the ruins of the former camp's crematorium.

In his remarks at the ceremony, reported by PAP news agency, Israel's ambassador to Poland Gershon Zohar recalled the words of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Eli Wiesel: "Not all the victims were Jews, but all Jews were victims."
Over the past weekend, the young Jews have been visiting Holocaust memorials and Jewish cultural sites in Warsaw and other cities.
